Rozas el cristal de tu móvil y sabe en q: You brush the glass of your phone and it knows exactly where you touched, even with several fingers, but it does not respond to a fingernail or a wool glove. There are no buttons or pressure: the finger changes by a few picofarads the capacitance of a capacitor under the glass.

La yema del dedo y el electrodo de debaj: The fingertip and the electrode below are the two plates of a parallel-plate capacitor, and the glass is its dielectric. That tool gives the capacitance, the charge at 3.3 V and even the field inside the glass, and lets you add another layer (a glove) to see how the capacitance falls.
Se abre con una yema y un electrodo de 5: It opens with a fingertip and a 5 × 5 mm electrode separated by 0.7 mm of glass with εr = 7 and 3.3 V: we get 2.21 pF and 7.3 pC. Add a 1 mm layer with εr = 3 and check that the capacitance drops to a quarter.

Debajo del cristal de tu móvil hay dos c: Under the glass of your phone there are two layers of strips of a material that conducts and is transparent (indium tin oxide). Some are **rows** and the others **columns**, separated by an insulator, and each crossing is a small **capacitor**.\n\nA controller chip sends a pulse along each row and measures what arrives along each column, hundreds of times per second. While nothing touches the glass, each crossing always holds the same charge. To know where you have touched, it is enough to find the crossing where something changes.
El dedo es un conductor, y la pantalla l: The finger is a conductor, and the screen notices
de tu cuerpo es agua con sales disueltas: of your body is water with dissolved salts, which conducts electricity.
Tu cuerpo es en su mayor parte agua con: Your body is mostly water with salts, and that makes it a good conductor. It is also connected to ground through you and what you touch.\n\nWhen you rest your fingertip on the glass, the finger (a conductor) and the electrode underneath (another conductor), separated by the glass (an insulator), are exactly what is needed for a **capacitor**. Neither the glass nor the electrodes change: what changes is that there is now one more conductor nearby.
La capacidad del dedo con el electrodo: The capacitance of the finger with the electrode
es la capacidad entre la yema y un elect: is the capacitance between the fingertip and a 5 × 5 mm electrode, with the glass in between.
Es un condensador plano, y se calcula co:
It is a parallel-plate capacitor, and is calculated as usual: $C = {ε_0 ε_r S}/d$. With an electrode of $S = 5 × 5 "mm" = 25 "mm"^2$, glass of $d = 0.7 "mm"$ and $ε_r = 7$:

$C = {8.854·10^{−12} · 7 · 25·10^{−6}}/{0.7·10^{−3}} = ${f2(datos.Cd * 1e12)} "pF"$

A capacitance of a few picofarads, very small, but measurable. The thinner the glass or the higher its $ε_r$, the larger it is: that is why screens use thin glass and not a thick case.
El controlador detecta cuánta carga cabe: The controller detects how much charge fits
sube la capacidad del electrodo al apoya: the capacitance of the electrode rises when the finger rests on it: from ${pF(CS0)} to ${pF(CS0 + datos.Cd)}.
Cada electrodo tiene ya una capacidad pr: Each electrode already has its own capacitance, of about $${f0(CS0 * 1e12)} "pF"$. The finger adds its own **in parallel**, so they **add up**: $C = ${f0(CS0 * 1e12)} + ${f2(datos.Cd * 1e12)} = ${f2((CS0 + datos.Cd) * 1e12)} "pF"$.\n\nThe controller charges the electrode to $V = ${f1(V)} "V"$ and measures the charge that fits: $Q = C V$ goes from ${pC(datos.Q0)} to ${pC(datos.Q1)}. If the increase exceeds a threshold, there is a touch. (Today's screens actually measure the *mutual* capacitance of each crossing, which *drops* a little because the finger takes away part of the field lines, but it is the same kind of change of a few picofarads.)
La posición: el centro de gravedad de la: The position: the centre of gravity of the signals
de error al situar el dedo, aunque los e: of error in locating the finger, even though the electrodes are every 5 mm.
Un dedo mide más de 5 mm de ancho, así q:
A finger is more than 5 mm wide, so it touches several electrodes at once and changes the signal of each in proportion to how close it is. With the signals of the neighbours the chip calculates the **centre of gravity**:

$x = {Σ x_i s_i}/{Σ s_i}$

That way an electrode is not needed for every point: with electrodes every 5 mm the finger is located to a precision of less than 1 mm. With several crossings showing a signal at once, the screen also tracks several fingers (multitouch).
queda con un guante de 1 mm: unas 4 vece: remains with a 1 mm glove: about 4 times less than with a bare finger.
Un guante es una capa más de aislante en: A glove is one more layer of insulator between the finger and the electrode, in series with the glass: $d_"eff" = d_1/ε_{r1} + d_2/ε_{r2}$. With a 1 mm wool glove ($ε_r ≈ 3$): $C = {ε_0 S}/{0.7/7 + 1/3} = ${f2(datos.C1mm * 1e12)} "pF"$, which no longer reaches the assumed threshold of 1 pF.\n\nA fingernail, a pencil or an ordinary wool glove do not work because they do not conduct or are too far away. "Touch" gloves have conductive thread in the fingertips, and stylus pens for screens have a conductive tip. And a drop of water is noticed: water conducts.
